title: 3D Part Segmentation for Reconstructed Plant Models via Targeted 2D-Guided Refinement
abstract:
Organ-level segmentation of 3D plant models reconstructed from real plants is a prerequisite for phenotypic measurements such as organ counting, morphology estimation, and structural analysis. 
However, plant meshes are challenging for general-purpose 3D part segmentation because they contain thin structures, repeated and self-similar organs, frequent contact between neighbouring components, and weak attachment boundaries. 
As a result, one-shot part segmentation can merge multiple organs into coarse predictions, limiting downstream organ-level analysis.
This paper presents a novel refinement strategy to improve a 3D part segmentation workflow for challenging plant meshes, and to repair such under-segmented predictions.
Starting from a general-purpose 3D part-segmentation workflow, each predicted part is rendered from six canonical views and analysed using the Segment Anything Model. 
Multi-view mask voting selects likely under-segmented parent parts for one additional 3D segmentation pass, while unselected parts remain unchanged. 
Surface-normal, wireframe, and depth renderings are compared as geometry-to-image encodings.
The pipeline is evaluated on 14 bean meshes with 202 manually annotated parts, including four real-derived meshes reconstructed from images of real bean plants and ten procedural L-system meshes. 
The one-shot workflow recovers 73.8\% of annotated parts without plant-specific training.
Surface-normal-guided refinement modifies only 5 of 251 one-shot predictions, yet increases GT-correct recovery to 75.3\%, and reduces under-segmented parts from 24.6\% to 18.5\% on the real-derived subset.
These results suggest that 2D foundation-model guidance can provide a selective and practical repair mechanism for plant-specific 3D part segmentation.
